renders._yaml:
- component: advanced_viz
  id: isomir_classes
  title: isomiR classes per sample
  description: |-
    Each bar is a sample, split into the classes of one partition of its miRNA reads, such as the state of the 3' end or the 5' end. It answers how much of each sample's miRNA reads matches the reference sequence and how the rest differs.
    How to read: switch the partition with the rank control. A shifted 5' end moves the seed region and with it the targets. Compare samples or groups, since a class that differs between conditions is worth following up in the landscape tile.
    Note: a nucleotide change cannot be told from an editing event, a SNP or a sequencing error, and a change seen in one sample only is most likely an error.
    Source: https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/31504201/
  kind: stacked_bar
  config:
    x_title: Sample
    value_title: Share of miRNA reads
    legend_pos: bottom
  roles:
    sample_id: sample
    taxon: taxon
    rank: rank
    abundance: abundance

- component: interactive
  title: isomiR class filter
  description: Pick one or more isomiR classes to keep. It filters the tiles of the dashboard that read
    this table.
  interactive_type: MultiSelect
  column_name: taxon

- component: table
  title: isomiR class table
  description: |-
    Each row is a sample, a partition and a class, with the reads in the class and their percentage of the sample's miRNA reads. It answers how many reads fall in each isomiR class.
    How to read: filter by partition, sort by percentage to find the dominant classes, and compare samples of different groups.

outputs.name: isomiR landscape of the top miRNAs

renders._yaml:
- component: advanced_viz
  id: isomir_dot_plot
  title: isomiR classes of the top miRNAs
  description: |-
    Each dot is a miRNA in one isomiR class: its colour is the mean share of the miRNA's reads in that class and its size is the fraction of samples where the class is a real part of the reads. It answers which isomiR forms each abundant miRNA carries and whether they are the same across samples.
    How to read: a large dark dot is a class that holds many reads in most samples, such as a miRNA that is mostly 3' trimmed everywhere. A small dot with a dark colour is a class that is common in only part of the cohort, so look at the samples behind it. The classes are not exclusive, since one read can be 3' trimmed and carry an addition.
    Lines and annotations: a class counts as present in a sample when it holds at least 5 percent of that miRNA's reads there, and only samples with at least 10 reads of the miRNA are counted. Both are settings of the recipe, not published cut-offs.
    Source: https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/31504201/
  kind: dot_plot
  roles:
    cluster: variant_class
    gene: mirna
    mean_expression: mean_share_pct
    frac_expressing: samples_fraction

- component: table
  title: isomiR landscape table
  description: |-
    Each row is a miRNA in one isomiR class, with the mean share of its reads, the fraction of samples where the class is present, the reads in the class and the miRNA's expression rank. It answers how common each class is for each miRNA.
    How to read: sort by mean share to find the dominant forms, and filter on a miRNA to read all its classes.

- component: figure
  title: miRNA expression distribution
  description: |-
    Each box is a miRNA, summarising its expression across samples as log2 of counts per million miRNA-assigned reads, with every sample drawn as a point. It answers how abundant each miRNA is and how much it varies between samples.
    How to read: boxes higher up are more abundant miRNAs. A wide box or a point far from the rest marks a miRNA or a sample that varies, so check that sample in the PCA. The scale is relative, so it follows the sample's total of miRNA reads.
    Lines and annotations: The dashed line is the median expression (log2 CPM) of this table, a reference computed from the rows on show (it follows the filters), not a cut-off of mirtop.
  visu_type: box
  dict_kwargs:
    x: mirna
    y: log2_cpm
    points: all
    labels:
      mirna: miRNA
      log2_cpm: Expression (log2 CPM)
  reference_lines:
  - axis: y
    stat: median
    column: log2_cpm

- component: card
  title: Reads in the top miRNAs
  description: |-
    The hero number is the total of miRNA reads over the samples in view, and the bars rank the miRNAs that hold the most of them. It answers whether a few miRNAs dominate the library.
    How to read: miRNA libraries are often dominated by a handful of abundant miRNAs. When one miRNA holds most of the reads, the others are measured with fewer reads, so treat the low abundance ones with caution.
  column: reads
  aggregation: sum
  aggregations:
  - median
  - max
  secondary_layout: top_n
  breakdown_col: mirna
  top_n_count: 5
  caption: the five miRNAs with the most reads, with the median and largest per sample

- component: card
  title: miRNAs detected
  description: |-
    The hero number is the count of distinct miRNAs seen in the samples in view, and the bars rank the samples that have the most. It answers how many miRNAs the data detects.
    How to read: a sample with far fewer miRNAs than the rest points to a shallow or low-quality library. Open the PCA to see whether it also separates there.
  column: mirna
  aggregation: nunique
  aggregations:
  - count
  secondary_layout: top_n
  breakdown_col: sample
  top_n_count: 3
  caption: samples with the most miRNA rows, and the total of rows

- component: interactive
  title: miRNA filter
  description: Pick one or more miRNAs to keep. It filters the tiles of the dashboard that read this table.
  interactive_type: MultiSelect
  column_name: mirna

- component: interactive
  title: Expression range filter
  description: Set a range of log2 counts per million to keep. It filters the tiles of the dashboard that
    read this table.
  interactive_type: RangeSlider
  column_name: log2_cpm

- component: table
  title: miRNA counts table
  description: |-
    Each row is a miRNA in a sample, with its reads summed over its isomiRs, counts per million, their log2, the number of distinct isomiRs and the share of reads matching the reference sequence. It answers how much of each miRNA each sample holds.
    How to read: sort by reads or by the reference share, and filter on a miRNA or a sample to follow it.

- component: advanced_viz
  id: mirna_mean_variance
  title: miRNA mean and variation
  description: |-
    Each point is a miRNA: its mean expression across samples on the horizontal axis and the spread of that expression on the vertical axis, coloured by the arm it comes from and sized by the share of samples where it is detected. It answers which miRNAs are abundant and which vary most between samples.
    How to read: miRNAs high on the vertical axis vary the most, so they are the candidates to separate groups, while those far to the right are abundant. Small points are detected in few samples, and their spread is less reliable. The labelled points are the most variable ones.
  kind: scatter_xy
  config:
    x_title: Mean expression (log2 CPM)
    y_title: Standard deviation of expression (log2 CPM)
    top_n_labels: 10
    legend_pos: bottom
  roles:
    x: mean_log2_cpm
    y: sd_log2_cpm
    label: mirna
    color: arm
    size: detection_pct

- component: card
  title: miRNAs by arm
  description: |-
    The hero number is the count of distinct miRNAs, and the ring splits them by the arm of the hairpin they come from, 5p or 3p. It answers whether the expressed miRNAs come from one arm more than the other.
    How to read: both arms of a hairpin can be expressed, with one usually dominating. A ring heavily tilted to one arm in this table reflects the most abundant miRNAs.
  column: mirna
  aggregation: nunique
  aggregations:
  - count
  secondary_layout: donut
  breakdown_col: arm
  caption: split into 5p and 3p arms, with the total of rows

- component: card
  title: Reads matching the reference
  description: |-
    The hero number is the median percentage of a miRNA's reads that match its reference mature sequence exactly, and the box shows the quartiles over miRNAs. It answers how far reads differ from the reference.
    How to read: a low median means most reads are isomiRs, with trimmed or extended ends or added nucleotides, which is typical of small RNA data. Open the isomiR tiles to see the classes behind it.
  column: reference_pct
  aggregation: median
  aggregations:
  - box_plot_stats
  secondary_layout: box_plot
  caption: median, with its spread across miRNAs

- component: interactive
  title: Mean expression range filter
  description: Set a range of mean log2 counts per million to keep. It filters the tiles of the dashboard
    that read this table.
  interactive_type: RangeSlider
  column_name: mean_log2_cpm

- component: table
  title: miRNA summary table
  description: |-
    Each row is a miRNA, with its mean and median counts per million, the spread of its expression, the samples where it is detected, its isomiR diversity and the share of reads matching the reference. It answers which miRNAs to follow up, and a row selection filters the other tiles.
    How to read: sort by spread or by detection to find variable or rare miRNAs.
  row_selection_enabled: true
  row_selection_column: mirna

- component: advanced_viz
  id: mirna_group_compare
  title: Group comparison of miRNA expression
  description: |-
    Each point is a miRNA in a comparison of two groups of samples that you pick, with the fold change of its expression on the horizontal axis and the significance of the difference on the vertical axis. It answers which miRNAs separate the two groups.
    How to read: miRNAs in the upper left and upper right corners differ most between the groups, higher in one or the other. Choose groups with several samples each, since a single sample gives no estimate of variation, and treat a result from few samples as exploratory.
    Lines and annotations: the horizontal line is a false discovery rate of 0.05 and the vertical lines mark an absolute log2 fold change of 1. These are the tile's own defaults, and no source defines them for miRNA data.
  kind: group_compare
  config:
    top_n_labels: 10
  roles:
    index: sample

- component: table
  title: Expression matrix table
  description: |-
    Each row is a sample, with the counts per million of each of the most expressed miRNAs and the design columns. It answers what the input of the group comparison looks like.
    How to read: check that the design column holds the groups you intend to compare.

- component: advanced_viz
  id: mirna_pca
  title: Sample PCA of miRNA expression
  description: |-
    Each point is a sample, placed by the principal components of log2 counts per million (plus one) over the most variable expressed miRNAs, and coloured by its number of miRNA reads. It answers whether samples group by biology or by sequencing depth.
    How to read: samples of the same condition should sit together. When the colour gradient runs along a component, depth drives the separation and not the design, so normalise or drop shallow libraries. A sample far from its group is a candidate outlier.
  kind: embedding
  config:
    axis_prefix: PC
    legend_pos: right
  roles:
    sample_id: sample
    dim_1: dim_1
    dim_2: dim_2
    dim_3: dim_3
    color: mirna_reads

- component: card
  title: miRNAs detected per sample
  description: |-
    The hero number is the median count of miRNAs detected per sample, and the box shows the quartiles. It answers how complex the libraries are.
    How to read: a sample with far fewer miRNAs than the rest points to a shallow or degraded library. Compare it with its miRNA reads in the PCA colours.
  column: mirnas_detected
  aggregation: median
  aggregations:
  - box_plot_stats
  secondary_layout: box_plot
  caption: median, with its spread across samples

- component: table
  title: Sample PCA table
  description: |-
    Each row is a sample with its principal components, its number of miRNA reads and its number of detected miRNAs. It answers which samples are outliers on a component.
    How to read: sort by a component to find the extremes, and compare reads with detected miRNAs to tell depth from design.

- component: advanced_viz
  id: top_variable_mirna_heatmap
  title: Most variable miRNAs
  description: |-
    Each cell is the expression of one miRNA in one sample, as log2 counts per million plus one, for the most variable expressed miRNAs. It answers which miRNAs vary across samples and which samples resemble each other.
    How to read: rows and columns are clustered, so samples of one condition should fall into the same block, with a block of miRNAs that is high in that block of samples. A sample that clusters apart from its group is a candidate outlier. When the design columns are given, they are drawn as annotations above the columns.
  kind: complex_heatmap
  roles:
    index: mirna

- component: table
  title: Most variable miRNAs table
  description: |-
    Each row is a miRNA, with its log2 expression in every sample. It answers the exact values behind the heatmap.
    How to read: sort a sample column to find its highest miRNAs.

- component: advanced_viz
  id: isomir_classes
  title: isomiR classes per sample
  description: |-
    Each bar is a sample, split into the classes of one partition of its miRNA reads, such as the state of the 3' end or the 5' end. It answers how much of each sample's miRNA reads matches the reference sequence and how the rest differs.

  config:
    x_title: Sample
    value_title: Share of miRNA reads
    legend_pos: bottom

    sample_id: sample
    taxon: taxon
    rank: rank
    abundance: abundance

- component: interactive
  title: isomiR class filter
  description: Pick one or more isomiR classes to keep. It filters the tiles of the dashboard that read
    this table.
  interactive_type: MultiSelect
  column_name: taxon

    Lines and annotations: The dashed line is the median expression (log2 CPM) of this table, a reference computed from the rows on show (it follows the filters), not a cut-off of mirtop.
  visu_type: box
  dict_kwargs:
    x: mirna
    y: log2_cpm
    points: all
    labels:
      mirna: miRNA
      log2_cpm: Expression (log2 CPM)
  reference_lines:
  - axis: y
    stat: median
    column: log2_cpm

- component: card
  title: Reads in the top miRNAs
  description: |-
    The hero number is the total of miRNA reads over the samples in view, and the bars rank the miRNAs that hold the most of them. It answers whether a few miRNAs dominate the library.
    How to read: miRNA libraries are often dominated by a handful of abundant miRNAs. When one miRNA holds most of the reads, the others are measured with fewer reads, so treat the low abundance ones with caution.
  column: reads
  aggregation: sum
  aggregations:
  - median
  - max
  secondary_layout: top_n
  breakdown_col: mirna
  top_n_count: 5
  caption: the five miRNAs with the most reads, with the median and largest per sample

- component: card
  title: miRNAs detected
  description: |-
    The hero number is the count of distinct miRNAs seen in the samples in view, and the bars rank the samples that have the most. It answers how many miRNAs the data detects.
    How to read: a sample with far fewer miRNAs than the rest points to a shallow or low-quality library. Open the PCA to see whether it also separates there.
  column: mirna
  aggregation: nunique
  aggregations:
  - count
  secondary_layout: top_n
  breakdown_col: sample
  top_n_count: 3
  caption: samples with the most miRNA rows, and the total of rows

- component: interactive
  title: miRNA filter
  description: Pick one or more miRNAs to keep. It filters the tiles of the dashboard that read this table.
  interactive_type: MultiSelect
  column_name: mirna

- component: interactive
  title: Expression range filter
  description: Set a range of log2 counts per million to keep. It filters the tiles of the dashboard that
    read this table.
  interactive_type: RangeSlider
  column_name: log2_cpm

- component: table
  title: miRNA counts table
  description: |-
    Each row is a miRNA in a sample, with its reads summed over its isomiRs, counts per million, their log2, the number of distinct isomiRs and the share of reads matching the reference sequence. It answers how much of each miRNA each sample holds.
    How to read: sort by reads or by the reference share, and filter on a miRNA or a sample to follow it.

- component: advanced_viz
  id: mirna_mean_variance
  title: miRNA mean and variation
  description: |-
    Each point is a miRNA: its mean expression across samples on the horizontal axis and the spread of that expression on the vertical axis, coloured by the arm it comes from and sized by the share of samples where it is detected. It answers which miRNAs are abundant and which vary most between samples.
    How to read: miRNAs high on the vertical axis vary the most, so they are the candidates to separate groups, while those far to the right are abundant. Small points are detected in few samples, and their spread is less reliable. The labelled points are the most variable ones.
  kind: scatter_xy
  config:
    x_title: Mean expression (log2 CPM)
    y_title: Standard deviation of expression (log2 CPM)
    top_n_labels: 10
    legend_pos: bottom
  roles:
    x: mean_log2_cpm
    y: sd_log2_cpm
    label: mirna
    color: arm
    size: detection_pct

- component: card
  title: miRNAs by arm
  description: |-
    The hero number is the count of distinct miRNAs, and the ring splits them by the arm of the hairpin they come from, 5p or 3p. It answers whether the expressed miRNAs come from one arm more than the other.
    How to read: both arms of a hairpin can be expressed, with one usually dominating. A ring heavily tilted to one arm in this table reflects the most abundant miRNAs.
  column: mirna
  aggregation: nunique
  aggregations:
  - count
  secondary_layout: donut
  breakdown_col: arm
  caption: split into 5p and 3p arms, with the total of rows

- component: card
  title: Reads matching the reference
  description: |-
    The hero number is the median percentage of a miRNA's reads that match its reference mature sequence exactly, and the box shows the quartiles over miRNAs. It answers how far reads differ from the reference.
    How to read: a low median means most reads are isomiRs, with trimmed or extended ends or added nucleotides, which is typical of small RNA data. Open the isomiR tiles to see the classes behind it.
  column: reference_pct
  aggregation: median
  aggregations:
  - box_plot_stats
  secondary_layout: box_plot
  caption: median, with its spread across miRNAs

- component: interactive
  title: Mean expression range filter
  description: Set a range of mean log2 counts per million to keep. It filters the tiles of the dashboard
    that read this table.
  interactive_type: RangeSlider
  column_name: mean_log2_cpm

- component: table
  title: miRNA summary table
  description: |-
    Each row is a miRNA, with its mean and median counts per million, the spread of its expression, the samples where it is detected, its isomiR diversity and the share of reads matching the reference. It answers which miRNAs to follow up, and a row selection filters the other tiles.
    How to read: sort by spread or by detection to find variable or rare miRNAs.
  row_selection_enabled: true
  row_selection_column: mirna

- component: advanced_viz
  id: mirna_group_compare
  title: Group comparison of miRNA expression
  description: |-
    Each point is a miRNA in a comparison of two groups of samples that you pick, with the fold change of its expression on the horizontal axis and the significance of the difference on the vertical axis. It answers which miRNAs separate the two groups.
    How to read: miRNAs in the upper left and upper right corners differ most between the groups, higher in one or the other. Choose groups with several samples each, since a single sample gives no estimate of variation, and treat a result from few samples as exploratory.
    Lines and annotations: the horizontal line is a false discovery rate of 0.05 and the vertical lines mark an absolute log2 fold change of 1. These are the tile's own defaults, and no source defines them for miRNA data.
  kind: group_compare
  config:
    top_n_labels: 10
  roles:
    index: sample

- component: table
  title: Expression matrix table
  description: |-
    Each row is a sample, with the counts per million of each of the most expressed miRNAs and the design columns. It answers what the input of the group comparison looks like.
    How to read: check that the design column holds the groups you intend to compare.

- component: advanced_viz
  id: mirna_pca
  title: Sample PCA of miRNA expression
  description: |-
    Each point is a sample, placed by the principal components of log2 counts per million (plus one) over the most variable expressed miRNAs, and coloured by its number of miRNA reads. It answers whether samples group by biology or by sequencing depth.
    How to read: samples of the same condition should sit together. When the colour gradient runs along a component, depth drives the separation and not the design, so normalise or drop shallow libraries. A sample far from its group is a candidate outlier.
  kind: embedding
  config:
    axis_prefix: PC
    legend_pos: right
  roles:
    sample_id: sample
    dim_1: dim_1
    dim_2: dim_2
    dim_3: dim_3
    color: mirna_reads

- component: card
  title: miRNAs detected per sample
  description: |-
    The hero number is the median count of miRNAs detected per sample, and the box shows the quartiles. It answers how complex the libraries are.
    How to read: a sample with far fewer miRNAs than the rest points to a shallow or degraded library. Compare it with its miRNA reads in the PCA colours.
  column: mirnas_detected
  aggregation: median
  aggregations:
  - box_plot_stats
  secondary_layout: box_plot
  caption: median, with its spread across samples

- component: table
  title: Sample PCA table
  description: |-
    Each row is a sample with its principal components, its number of miRNA reads and its number of detected miRNAs. It answers which samples are outliers on a component.
    How to read: sort by a component to find the extremes, and compare reads with detected miRNAs to tell depth from design.

- component: advanced_viz
  id: top_variable_mirna_heatmap
  title: Most variable miRNAs
  description: |-
    Each cell is the expression of one miRNA in one sample, as log2 counts per million plus one, for the most variable expressed miRNAs. It answers which miRNAs vary across samples and which samples resemble each other.
    How to read: rows and columns are clustered, so samples of one condition should fall into the same block, with a block of miRNAs that is high in that block of samples. A sample that clusters apart from its group is a candidate outlier. When the design columns are given, they are drawn as annotations above the columns.
  kind: complex_heatmap
  roles:
    index: mirna

- component: table
  title: Most variable miRNAs table
  description: |-
    Each row is a miRNA, with its log2 expression in every sample. It answers the exact values behind the heatmap.
    How to read: sort a sample column to find its highest miRNAs.
